{"artifact":"SmeDossierEnvelope","schema_version":"0.4.0","stage_id":"02.dossier_sections","probe":"rdmv-sd-x","lineage":{"input_manifest_sha256":"e7c937148ef4d226f675c59cbf424d30e4113b8467d8f9c710cd9ed20d574d07","candidate_lineage_id":"2026-10-28-rdmv-sd-class-std:lineage:37","source_registry_sha256":"a4e51960bfe4da242ea11046073ac8d3d0353ce120a5409a11c1f9ab4c4da57a","source_liveness_sha256":"1aea607665fc1312b9a6988c94545b32e414886d6d428b2b6d66e4261f9397f1"},"envelope_scope":{"kind":"partial_chunk","assigned_section_ids":["C"],"chunk_index":1,"chunk_total":1},"section_char_limit":12000,"sections":[{"section_id":"C","chunk_id":"C.01","merge_seq":1,"domain":"Right of way, signals and signs","heading":"C — Knowledge dossier: Right of way, signals and signs","learner_facing":true,"markdown":"## C — Knowledge dossier: Right of way, signals and signs

FACT_ID: sec09-F01 | anchor: A31
Right-of-way rules guide yielding and the order of entry, but drivers must consider the actual situation rather than assume priority automatically. [A31]
Source: [A31 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0031]

FACT_ID: sec09-F02 | anchor: A31
Yield to a driver already at the intersection or arriving there before you. [A31]
Source: [A31 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0031]

FACT_ID: sec09-F03 | anchor: A31
When turning left, yield to traffic approaching in the opposite lane. [A31]
Source: [A31 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0031]

FACT_ID: sec09-F04 | anchor: A31
At an all-way stop, drivers who arrive simultaneously must yield to the driver on the right. [A31]
Source: [A31 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0031]

FACT_ID: sec09-F05 | anchor: A31
When entering a public highway from a driveway or private road, yield to highway traffic. [A31]
Source: [A31 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0031]

FACT_ID: sec09-F06 | anchor: A31
A driver on an entrance or acceleration ramp must yield to vehicles already on the limited-access or interstate highway. [A31]
Source: [A31 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0031]

FACT_ID: sec09-F07 | anchor: A31
Yield to pedestrians, bicyclists and drivers still within the intersection. [A31]
Source: [A31 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0031]

FACT_ID: sec09-F08 | anchor: A31
The funeral-procession rule says only its first vehicle must obey traffic signs and signals. [A31]
Source: [A31 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0031]

FACT_ID: sec09-F09 | anchor: A31
Vehicles in a funeral procession must use their headlights, and other drivers must not cut into or interfere with the procession. [A31]
Source: [A31 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0031]

FACT_ID: sec09-F10 | anchor: A31
Traffic-control devices include signals, signs, road markings and directions from police, highway workers and school crossing guards. [A31]
Source: [A31 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0031]

FACT_ID: sec09-F11 | anchor: A31
A pedestrian hybrid beacon helps people cross busy or faster roads at midblock crossings and uncontrolled intersections. [A31]
Source: [A31 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0031]

FACT_ID: sec09-F12 | anchor: A31
The pedestrian hybrid beacon described in the handbook has 2 red lenses above 1 yellow lens. [A31]
Source: [A31 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0031]

FACT_ID: sec09-F13 | anchor: A31
A pedestrian hybrid beacon stays dark until a pedestrian presses the call button. [A31]
Source: [A31 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0031]

FACT_ID: sec09-F14 | anchor: A31
After activation, the beacon follows a yellow-to-red sequence with steady and flashing lights directing motorists to slow and stop. [A31]
Source: [A31 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0031]

FACT_ID: sec09-F15 | anchor: A31
The handbook says the pedestrian display then flashes WALK and the beacon returns dark after the pedestrian crosses safely. [A31]
Source: [A31 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0031]

FACT_ID: sec09-F16 | anchor: A32
Vertical traffic signals normally show red above yellow above green, while horizontal signals place red left, yellow center and green right. [A32]
Source: [A32 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0032]

FACT_ID: sec09-F17 | anchor: A32
A steady red signal requires a complete stop and waiting for green and clear crossing traffic before proceeding straight. [A32]
Source: [A32 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0032]

FACT_ID: sec09-F18 | anchor: A32
A right turn on red is allowed only after stopping completely when safe and when no sign forbids the turn. [A32]
Source: [A32 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0032]

FACT_ID: sec09-F19 | anchor: A32
Before turning on red, yield to pedestrians, bicyclists and vehicles, then turn safely while remaining in the proper lane. [A32]
Source: [A32 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0032]

FACT_ID: sec09-F20 | anchor: A32
A flashing red light is treated like a stop sign: stop fully, then continue only when safe. [A32]
Source: [A32 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0032]

FACT_ID: sec09-F21 | anchor: A32
A red arrow prohibits movement in its direction until it goes out and a green arrow or green light appears. [A32]
Source: [A32 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0032]

FACT_ID: sec09-F22 | anchor: A32
A steady yellow light warns that red is next and requires stopping when stopping is safe. [A32]
Source: [A32 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0032]

FACT_ID: sec09-F23 | anchor: A32
If yellow appears after the vehicle is already in the intersection, continue through instead of stopping there. [A32]
Source: [A32 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0032]

FACT_ID: sec09-F24 | anchor: A32
A flashing yellow signal calls for reduced speed and caution. [A32]
Source: [A32 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0032]

FACT_ID: sec09-F25 | anchor: A32
A yellow arrow means protected turning is ending, so prepare to stop and yield to oncoming traffic before turning. [A32]
Source: [A32 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0032]

FACT_ID: sec09-F26 | anchor: A32
A flashing yellow left arrow permits a cautious left turn only when safe after yielding to oncoming traffic and pedestrians. [A32]
Source: [A32 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0032]

FACT_ID: sec09-F27 | anchor: A32
Oncoming traffic has a green signal while the described flashing-yellow left arrow is displayed. [A32]
Source: [A32 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0032]

FACT_ID: sec09-F28 | anchor: A32
A steady green permits proceeding but does not remove duties to yield to emergency vehicles and others required by law. [A32]
Source: [A32 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0032]

FACT_ID: sec09-F29 | anchor: A32
When a stopped driver receives green, crossing traffic must clear before the driver enters. [A32]
Source: [A32 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0032]

FACT_ID: sec09-F30 | anchor: A32
A left turn on a steady green is allowed only when safe, with oncoming traffic having priority and any left-turn prohibition still obeyed. [A32]
Source: [A32 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0032]

FACT_ID: sec09-F31 | anchor: A32
During a right or left turn, watch for pedestrians crossing in front of the vehicle. [A32]
Source: [A32 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0032]

FACT_ID: sec09-F32 | anchor: A32
A green arrow permits turning in its indicated direction, with no oncoming or crossing traffic expected during that arrow. [A32]
Source: [A32 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0032]

FACT_ID: sec09-F33 | anchor: A32
When a signal malfunctions, a driver facing green may proceed cautiously under SDCL 32-28-2. [A32]
Source: [A32 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0032]

FACT_ID: sec09-F34 | anchor: A32
When a signal malfunctions, a driver facing yellow may proceed cautiously under SDCL 32-28-3. [A32]
Source: [A32 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0032]

FACT_ID: sec09-F35 | anchor: A32
A red or completely dark malfunctioning signal must be treated as a stop sign. [A32]
Source: [A32 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0032]

Misconceptions: Green does not erase yielding duties, a flashing yellow arrow is not a protected turn, and a posted maximum is not safe in every weather condition.
Mnemonics: Use device, displayed state, required action and other road users as an authored decision cue.
Glossary: A crossbuck identifies a rail crossing; an ENS sign supplies railroad contact and location identifiers; regulatory signs state rules while warning signs announce hazards.
Dynamic facts: Local control devices and work zones vary by place and time. No location-specific sign or image-only symbol meaning is inferred.
